subject: Compute bursary request — OpenMaps: summer data import
messages:
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah@openmaps.org>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: compute bursary for summer import

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re well — I’m Sarah, maintainer for the OpenMaps core-data-import project. We run a small collective of volunteers and next month we’re coordinating a large community-driven data import (public government GIS -> vector tiles). The import will require a reliable inference engine to run a few preprocessing and tagging steps on many text/geodata records.

We’ve used free trial credits from a couple of providers before, but the scale here would burn through them quickly. Would Redwood consider a compute bursary or promo extension (credits + short trial extension) for OpenMaps? We can provide a brief mutual action plan and agree to public attribution in our sprint notes.

Quick facts:
- org: OpenMaps (nonprofit)
- repo: https://github.com/openmaps/core-data-import
- contributors: ~25 active for this sprint
- duration: 3 weeks (Nov 10–30)
- ask: ~$2k equivalent in tokens / 2 additional weeks trial extension

Happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk through the workload and share the repo/usage patterns.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Bennett
OpenMaps Project — Lead Maintainer
@sben_net

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah@openmaps.org>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: compute bursary for summer import

Thanks for the note, Sarah — appreciate the context and the early heads-up. Quick questions to help us evaluate:

1) Can you share a short-runbook or sample input size (records/day, avg tokens per record)?
2) Any NDAs or data-sensitivity concerns (PII, restricted sources)?
3) Would you be open to a short case study or a public blurb on our community grants page if we provide support?

Jonas — I’m looping you in for approvals on the community credits program (this looks like the type of maintainer ask we prioritize). If you need billing details or to route to Marcus for legal/terms, please advise.

If it’s easier, Sarah — we can set up a 20-min call Wed morning.

—
Marissa Cole
Developer Relations — Community Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: compute bursary for summer import

Marissa — saw this thread. High level: I’m comfortable approving a pilot bursary for a well-scoped community sprint. Proposed approach:

- Approve up to $2,000 in hosted credits (redeemable against Redwood API usage)
- Add a 2-week trial extension on top of the credit window
- Require a short MOU: usage window, expected spend cap (hard cap at $2k), and public attribution in sprint notes

Marcus/Neha — flag any procurement or compliance blockers. If not, I’ll greenlight and ask Marissa to issue an approval packet.

Jonas
VP Partnerships & Community

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:44:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: compute bursary for summer import

Thanks — a few operational notes before we commit:

- We need the repo link and confirmation that no sensitive/stored customer PII will be processed. Public government datasets are typically ok but we need a quick checkbox.
- Please confirm the billing contact and the HubSpot record so we can attach the MOU.
- Marcus: any legal review required for the MOU template? If OpenMaps signs a simple MOU (not a full contract), we can do a standard grant flow.

Marissa — once Sarah confirms repo + PII answer, I can prep the credit grant and the onboarding checklist (license, expected endpoints, sample size).

—Neha
Director, Customer Programs

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah@openmaps.org>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 18:05:00 -0400
Subject: Approved: Redwood compute bursary + trial extension for OpenMaps (next steps)

Hi Sarah — good news: we’ve approved a compute bursary pilot for OpenMaps. Summary below and next steps.

What we approved:
- $2,000 in hosted Redwood API credits, active Nov 10–Dec 10 (hard cap).
- 2-week trial extension applied to your account beginning Nov 10 (total extension through Dec 24 for trial behavior features).
- Required public attribution: a one-paragraph blurb in sprint notes and a small logo attribution on the project README.

Attachments: approval packet + onboarding checklist attached. Please review and reply with:
- confirmation that the repo is public and does not process PII (we’ve checked https://github.com/openmaps/core-data-import),
- billing contact info (name + email), and
- preferred account email for issuing the promo code.

Promo details (example):
- promo code: OPENMAPS-REDWOOD-2026 (redeem via console before Dec 10)
- hard cap: $2,000
- trial extension: 14 days beyond standard trial window

If everything looks good I’ll ask Neha to publish the credit in our system and Marcus to attach the MOU (standard). We can also schedule a 30-min onboarding session to review rate limits and recommended batching for geodata preprocessing.

Thanks, and excited to see what your community builds.

Marissa Cole
Developer Relations — Community Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachments: compute_bursary_approval.pdf (PDF, 120KB); openmaps_onboarding_checklist.docx (DOCX, 45KB)
